inclusion_rule: Studies whose ledger text names intracranial or auditory-cortex recordings, a listening or perception condition, an acoustic representation (spectrogram, temporal modulation, envelope or vocoder features) and reconstruction, decoding or synthesis. The design of interest is the acoustic representation that the decoder reconstructs from neural activity during heard speech: auditory/linear spectrogram, temporal-modulation energy, envelope only, or vocoder parameters. Boundary: production-only synthesis studies and encoding-only studies admitted by the pattern are counted but are not heard-speech reconstruction; full-text design regexes overlap and are upper bounds; versions of one study count once.

usual_approach.design: spectrogram reconstruction target (auditory, linear or mel spectrogram)
usual_approach.note: full-text pattern counts over 64 unique ledger matches, all years (overlapping): spectrogram_target 24, vocoder_parameter_target 13, envelope_target 12, temporal_modulation_target 6 keys = 4 distinct studies after merging versions (the target; Martin et al. 2014 and Martin 2017 thesis, same lineage; Yang et al. 2015, which uses modulation space for evaluation). Slot-filled design values give n=1 each, so the pattern count is used.

read_fulltext.loc: Results, Subjective evaluation of the reconstruction accuracy
read_fulltext.quote: The DNN-vocoder combination achieved the best performance (75% accuracy), which is 67% higher than the baseline system (Linear regression with auditory spectrogram).

The specific measure we used was the degree to which a multivariate pattern classifier (L1 norm regularized logistic regression 17 ) was able to distinguish single-trial response patterns of the evoked cortical potentials.

read_fulltext.loc: Methods, Kalman Filter for Real-Time BMI
read_fulltext.quote: Specifically, the Kalman filter was used to predict the intended positions and velocities of the first two formant frequencies based on the current values of the normalized neural firing rates.
In this study, we examined human STG, a nonprimary auditory area, and found that a nonlinear modulation representation yielded the best overall reconstruction accuracy
The electrocorticogram (ECoG) was recorded using a customized 64-channel subdural cortical electrode microarray, with center-to-center distance of 4 mm
We compared the reconstructed spectrograms estimated with two different models: a linear regression model and a deep neural network.

In the current study we use a novel approach to speech restoration in which we decode continuous auditory parameters for a real-time speech synthesizer from neuronal activity in motor cortex during attempted speech.
were developed for predicting the ten LPC coefficients directly from ECoG gamma activity.
In general, decoders that were trained to predict mel-frequency values directly (Vanilla and GAN-D) achieved higher Pearson correlation between reconstructed and target spectrograms.
Evaluation of the intelligibility of the synthesized speech indicates that 80% of the words can be correctly recognized by human listeners.
speech spectrograms reconstructed based on cortical responses to the mixture of speakers reveal the salient spectral and temporal features of the attended speaker
with phoneme error rate (PER) at 28.6%, and human listeners were able to recognize 71.6% of the words in the re-synthesized speech.
